title: Association Rule Learning: Apriori, Eclat and FP-Growth
description: How association learning mines co-occurrence rules like 'customers who buy A also buy B', and how Apriori, Eclat and FP-Growth each find frequent itemsets.
content:
**Association** is an unsupervised learning technique used to discover relationships hidden in large datasets. At its core, it analyzes the co-occurrence of items in the data to identify rules such as "If a customer buys item A, they might also buy item B".

Popular applications of the association technique:
• Basket data analysis
• Web usage mining
• Medical diagnosis

**Apriori** relies on the principle that any subset of a frequent itemset must also be frequent.

How it works:
• It starts by scanning the dataset to count the occurrence of individual items (1-itemsets).
• It iteratively expands these sets to 2-itemsets, 3-itemsets and so on, using a breadth-first search approach.
• It prunes candidates that do not meet a minimum support threshold.
• Once frequent itemsets are identified, it generates rules and evaluates them using confidence and lift criteria.
• It utilizes a hash-tree structure to count candidate frequencies efficiently.

**Eclat (Equivalence Class Transformation)** works differently from Apriori in that it adopts a vertical data format rather than a horizontal one.

How it works:
• Each item is associated with the transaction IDs (TIDs) in which it appears.
• The support for an itemset is determined by intersecting the transaction ID lists of the items.
• It uses a depth-first search strategy, which generally makes the algorithm faster in scenarios where the dataset is dense and the TID lists are manageable.

**FP-Growth (Frequent Pattern Growth)** is the improved version of the Apriori algorithm.

How it works:
• Instead of generating candidate itemsets through multiple passes over the data, it uses a divide-and-conquer strategy.
• It relies on the frequent-pattern tree (FP-tree) data structure.

**Quick comparison:**
• Apriori - horizontal format, breadth-first expansion of itemsets with pruning by minimum support; rules evaluated by confidence and lift; hash-tree counting.
• Eclat - vertical format with transaction ID lists, depth-first search, support via intersecting TID lists; fast on dense datasets.
• FP-Growth - divide-and-conquer over an FP-tree; avoids candidate generation through multiple passes over the data.
